study: Industrial recommendation ranking structures on a fixed HSTU retrieval pool v1
status: Frozen before candidate-pool generation, model training, or GPU execution
research_question: How do canonical and modern industrial ranking structures compare when they rerank the same label-independent candidates produced by the already reproduced HSTU and SASRec retrievers?

ranking: official TransAct module plus a public-data ranking head
role_boundary.policy: Retrieval and ranking metrics are reported in separate tables. A ranker cannot recover a target absent from the fixed candidate pool.

din.implementation: Independent DIN-style PyTorch adaptation with candidate-conditioned local activation, softmax-normalized attention, PReLU activations, and no mini-batch-aware regularization. It is not a canonical DIN reproduction.

twin.implementation: Independent short-history structural adaptation using one shared relevance metric for GSU top-k selection and ESU attention.

data.dataset: MovieLens-1M prepared by the pinned HSTU preprocessor

split.training_positions: All positions before each user's last two events; deterministic user-balanced hash sample.
split.validation: Last event for a frozen deterministic 1000-user partition.
split.test: Last event for the complementary 5040 users.

data.event_semantics: Every rating event remains an interaction, matching the public HSTU task. Ratings are used only as action-type payloads and summary features.
data.statistics: Candidate popularity and recency normalization are fitted from training positions only. The persisted training maximum request gap is invariant to validation/test timestamps.

candidate_pool.construction: The fixed ranker pool is HSTU-large epoch100 exact full-catalog top500, excluding prior history and without target injection. HSTU, SASRec, and a rank-interleaved three-retriever union remain diagnostic retrieval outputs only.
candidate_pool.pilot_gate: A 100-user implementation pilot rejected a fixed-width three-way interleave because truncating the union could reduce an individual retriever's ceiling. HSTU-large was frozen from the prior immutable study before ranker execution. The same MovieLens last-event benchmark was used in that prior retriever comparison, so this extension is not a fresh holdout for retriever-family selection.

training.negative_source: Exact HSTU-large epoch100 full-catalog candidates for each training context; target removed after retrieval and retained only as the supervised positive.
training.checkpoint_policy: Epoch 0 is the exact frozen retrieval-rank prior. Best validation checkpoint is selected prospectively from epochs 0-10; full validation and test run once after selection.

models.common_reranking_contract: Every learned model predicts a residual over -log(HSTU-large retrieval rank). The residual scalar is initialized to zero, so epoch 0 exactly preserves the candidate order and a learned ranker is retained only if validation improves.

torchrec-dlrm.information: User ID, candidate ID, latest-history item ID, and four dense training-only summary features.

torchrec-dcn.information: Same as DLRM; three low-rank cross layers.

din.information: DIN-style candidate-conditioned softmax attention over up to 200 history item embeddings plus user embedding and dense summaries. This differs from canonical DIN's unnormalized interest-intensity aggregation, Dice activations, and mini-batch-aware regularization.

twin.information: Shared target-history relevance score for full-history top20 GSU selection and ESU softmax pooling.

transact.information: Unchanged official TransAct module over the most recent 50 item/rating/time actions, candidate embedding concatenation, and a learned batch user embedding in the ranking head.

quality_metrics: unconditional HR/NDCG where retrieval misses count as zero

efficiency.scoring_shape: batch16 x 200 candidates with exact history shape and precision

non_admitted.BST: Superseded in this finite matrix by official TransAct code; covered in research.
non_admitted.DIEN: Adds an auxiliary interest-extraction objective and AUGRU, expanding the matrix without official maintained code.
non_admitted.PinnerFormer: Dense all-action future objective and production batch embedding pipeline unavailable.
non_admitted.Monolith: Online-training system rather than a matched offline ranking architecture.
non_admitted.OneRec: The original production paper is arXiv:2502.18965. Its private Kuaishou production stack remains unavailable.
non_admitted.OpenOneRec: The later Apache-2.0 OpenOneRec research release provides foundation models, RecIF-Bench and a full-stack training pipeline, but its 1.7B/8B generative instruction-following task is not a matched candidate ranker for this finite MovieLens panel.
non_admitted.OneTrans: No public implementation at the reviewed paper version.

rejected_protocols.reason: Truncating a three-retriever interleave reduced HSTU-large candidate coverage.
Compressed NPZ arrays were decompressed on every batch and no epoch completed.
Second-last-event labels had been observed by the official HSTU autoregressive training split.
Random catalog negatives did not match the hard HSTU candidate distribution used at evaluation.
The protocol discarded the strong retrieval order and forced an uninitialized ranker to replace it.
Missing training targets were assigned rank 65 instead of using the final evaluation depth of 200.
Recency normalization scanned validation/test request times instead of fitting on training positions only.

interpretation.independent_retriever_holdout: Both validation and test use each user's last event, which the official HSTU training split never observes. Users are partitioned before ranker selection so the prior second-last-event leakage is excluded.
interpretation.retriever_selection_reuse: HSTU-large was selected before this extension from the completed HSTU benchmark on the same last-event task. Ranker selection/test users are disjoint, but retriever-family selection is not evaluated on a new dataset.
interpretation.astra_review: Exact GPT-6-Astra/MAX capability remains unavailable; no substitute is labeled Astra and no numeric one-million-token claim is made.
interpretation.substitute_review: GPT-6.1 Sol with MAX reasoning and long context independently reviewed implementation, numerical aggregates, provenance, and conclusions. Findings were fixed and the affected experiment matrix was rerun.
